blocks.text: Verses 1-8 place Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome at the open tomb, where they hear that Jesus has been raised and will go before the disciples and Peter to Galilee. The earliest recoverable form of Mark ends at verse 8, with the women fleeing in fear and saying nothing; it announces the resurrection but does not narrate an appearance of the risen Jesus. Verses 9-20 are an ancient, canonical, and widely received longer ending, yet their vocabulary, style, content, and manuscript distribution indicate that they were added later than the earliest recoverable Gospel. Other ancient endings and additions show that this abrupt close prompted continued transmission and discussion.

The signs described in verses 17-18 are not presented as permission for coercive conversion, religious violence, medical neglect, dangerous exorcism, snake handling, poison drinking, exploiting people for prosperity, setting apocalyptic dates, or testing God. That boundary matters when these striking lines are read or invoked.
